chapters.title: Visual Foundations
chapters.subtitle: See one change at a time

chapters.title: Logical Matrices
chapters.subtitle: Rows and columns hold the key

levels.title: Taking Turns
levels.explanation: Two shapes take turns: circle, square, circle, square… After a circle always comes a square.
hints: Look only at the shape of each figure.
Two shapes alternate; which one has just appeared?

levels.title: Colour Wheel
levels.explanation: The colour cycles navy → teal → gold and then starts again. Teal is followed by gold.
hints: The shape never changes — watch the colour.
Three colours repeat in the same order.

levels.title: Growing Circle
levels.explanation: The circle grows by the same amount at every step, so the next circle is one step larger than the last.
hints: Compare the size of neighbouring circles.
The growth is steady: each step adds the same amount.

levels.title: Counting Up
levels.explanation: One dot is added at every step: 1, 2, 3, 4… so the next figure has five dots.
hints: Count the dots in each figure.
How many dots are added each time?

levels.title: Quarter Turns
levels.explanation: The arrow turns a quarter turn (90°) clockwise at every step: right, down, left, up… then right again.
hints: Follow the direction the arrow points.
Each step is the same turn in the same direction.

levels.title: Fill Rhythm
levels.explanation: The fill repeats solid → striped → outlined. After striped comes outlined.
hints: The triangle itself never changes — look inside it.
Three fills repeat in order.

levels.title: One More Side
levels.explanation: Each shape has one more side than the one before: 3, 4, 5, 6 — so the next shape has 7 sides (a heptagon).
hints: Count the straight edges of each shape.
Triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon… what has one more side?

levels.title: Straight Edges
levels.prompt: Four figures share a hidden property. Which one does not?
levels.explanation: Every figure is a polygon made of straight edges — except the circle, which has none.
hints: Think about what each outline is made of.
Edges can be straight or curved.

levels.title: Corner to Corner
levels.explanation: The dot jumps clockwise from corner to corner: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, then top-left again.
hints: Watch where the dot is on the 3×3 board.
It only visits corners, always turning the same way.

levels.title: Big to Small
levels.prompt: The same change turns each figure into its partner. Which figure completes the last pair?
levels.explanation: Each figure shrinks and loses its fill: a large solid shape becomes a small outlined copy of the same shape.
hints: Compare the left and right circle: what changed?
Two things change: size and fill. The shape stays the same.

levels.title: Backwards Turn
levels.explanation: The arrow turns 45° counter-clockwise at every step: up, up-left, left, down-left… so next it points straight down.
hints: Which way is the arrow turning: clockwise or counter-clockwise?
Each step is an eighth of a turn.

levels.title: Musical Chairs
levels.explanation: Every shape moves one place to the left at each step, and the shape on the far left wraps around to the right.
hints: Follow a single shape, such as the circle.
Shapes leaving on one side come back on the other.

levels.title: Turn, Then Flip
levels.prompt: Apply every step in order. What is the result?
levels.explanation: Turning the flag 90° clockwise lays the pole along the top with the pennant hanging down at the right end; mirroring left–right then moves the pennant to the left end.
hints: Do one step at a time and picture the flag after each.
After the turn the pennant hangs down at one end. Which end is it on after the mirror?

levels.title: Which Way?
levels.prompt: Which rule turns every left figure into its right figure?
levels.explanation: Both figures turn a quarter turn counter-clockwise: the arrow goes from pointing up to pointing left.
hints: Look at where the tip of the arrow ends up.
Is the turn clockwise or counter-clockwise, and by how much?

levels.title: Passing Each Other
levels.explanation: The teal circle moves one cell clockwise around the board's edge each step, while the gold square moves one cell counter-clockwise.
hints: Track the circle and the square separately.
They travel around the edge in opposite directions.

levels.title: Spin and Switch
levels.explanation: Two rules work together: the arrow turns 90° clockwise each step, and its colour alternates navy, teal, navy, teal.
hints: Treat direction and colour as two separate patterns.
The colour flips every step; the arrow turns a quarter turn.

levels.title: Rise and Fall
levels.explanation: The navy circles increase by one while the teal squares decrease by one, so the total always stays five.
hints: Count the circles and the squares separately.
One group grows exactly as fast as the other shrinks.

levels.title: Opposite Spins
levels.explanation: The top arrow turns 90° clockwise each step while the bottom arrow turns 90° counter-clockwise.
hints: Follow the top arrow on its own, then the bottom arrow.
The two arrows turn by the same amount but in opposite directions.

levels.title: Replacement
levels.explanation: At each step one more triangle, from left to right, is replaced by a circle. Next all four are circles.
hints: Count circles and triangles.
Each step replaces exactly one shape.

levels.title: Orbit
levels.explanation: Two rules combine: the arrow moves one cell clockwise around the edge, and it turns 90° clockwise at every step.
hints: Separate the movement from the turning.
Position: one cell along the edge. Direction: a quarter turn.

levels.title: Mirror Image
levels.prompt: Which rule turns every left figure into its right figure?
levels.explanation: Each right-hand figure is the left-hand figure seen in a vertical mirror: left and right swap, top and bottom stay put.
hints: Which parts stayed where they were, and which moved?
The tops stay at the top, so this is not a turn.

levels.title: Balance
levels.prompt: Four figures share a hidden property. Which one does not?
levels.explanation: Four figures are mirror-symmetric about a vertical line through their centre. In the diamond figure the two dots sit on opposite diagonal corners, so its left and right halves do not match.
hints: Imagine folding each figure down the middle.
Do the left and right halves match exactly?

levels.title: Upside Down
levels.prompt: The same change turns each figure into its partner. Which figure completes the last pair?
levels.explanation: The pair is reflected in a horizontal mirror: everything at the top moves to the bottom and shapes flip vertically, while left and right stay put.
hints: Compare which corner each shape is in before and after.
Left stays left; top becomes bottom.

levels.title: Turn the Board
levels.prompt: Apply every step in order. What is the result?
levels.explanation: Rotating the whole board carries the arrow with it: from the top-middle it travels to the right-middle and points right. Moving down puts it in the bottom-right corner, and the mirror sends it to the bottom-left, pointing left.
hints: When the whole board turns, the arrow's position turns too.
Track position and direction separately after each step.

levels.title: Crossing Paths
levels.explanation: The teal circle moves one cell right each step and the gold square one cell down; both wrap around to the other side of the board when they reach the edge.
hints: Follow each shape separately.
When a shape leaves the board it re-enters on the opposite side.

levels.title: Turning Block
levels.explanation: The whole group of three pieces turns a quarter turn clockwise around the centre of the board at every step.
hints: Follow the coral circle around the board.
The pieces keep their arrangement; only the group turns.

levels.title: Half Turn
levels.prompt: Which rule turns every left figure into its right figure?
levels.explanation: Both figures are turned upside down by a half turn (180°). The arrow alone cannot tell a half turn from a top–bottom mirror, but the flag can: its pennant points left afterwards, so it was turned rather than mirrored.
hints: Use the flag: which way does the pennant point afterwards?
A mirror never changes which way a pennant faces along the mirror line.

levels.title: Back Where It Started?
levels.prompt: Apply every step in order. What is the result?
levels.explanation: Turn, mirror, turn: the two quarter turns cancel out through the mirror, so the overall effect is a single left–right mirror of the original flag.
hints: Apply the steps one by one with care.
Compare your result with the original flag: what single change would do the same?

levels.title: Above and Below
levels.prompt: Four figures share a hidden property. Which one does not?
levels.explanation: In four figures the circle is higher than the triangle. In one figure the circle sits below the triangle.
hints: Ignore left and right; compare heights.
Where is the circle relative to the triangle?

levels.title: Three Moves, One Turn
levels.prompt: Apply every step in order. What is the result?
levels.explanation: Mirror left–right, turn 90° counter-clockwise, then mirror top–bottom. Combined, these three moves are equivalent to a single quarter turn counter-clockwise.
hints: Track the flag through each step, then place the two small shapes.
Two mirrors applied one after the other always add up to a turn.

levels.title: Rows and Columns
levels.explanation: Each row keeps the same shape, and each column keeps the same colour. The missing cell is in the square row and the teal column.
hints: What do the figures in the top row have in common?
Now look down each column.

levels.title: Quarter Turn Across
levels.prompt: The arrow changes into its partner. Apply the same change to the flag.
levels.explanation: The arrow turns a quarter turn clockwise to become its partner. The upside-down flag gets the same quarter turn, so it ends up pointing left with its pole along the top.
hints: What happens to the arrow between the two figures?
Apply exactly the same change to the flag.

levels.title: Shape by Row, Count by Column
levels.explanation: Every row uses one shape; every column has one more item than the column to its left (1, 2, 3).
hints: Read the rows first, then the columns.
The bottom row uses triangles. How many items does the third column have?

levels.title: Each Once
levels.explanation: Every row and every column contains a circle, a square and a triangle exactly once. The bottom row already has a triangle and a circle.
hints: Which shapes already appear in the last row?
Each shape appears exactly once per row.

levels.title: Shape Rows, Fill Pattern
levels.explanation: Each row uses a single shape, and each row and column contains solid, striped and outlined fills once each. The middle row is diamonds and is missing its solid fill.
hints: Separate the shape rule from the fill rule.
Which fill is missing from the middle row?

levels.title: Adding Up
levels.explanation: In every row, the number of dots in the third cell equals the dots in the first two cells added together: 1+2=3, 2+2=4, 3+1=4.
hints: Count the dots in each cell of the top row.
How could the first two numbers produce the third?

levels.title: Turning Grid
levels.explanation: Along each row the arrow turns 45° clockwise per step; down each column it turns 90° clockwise. From the bottom-left cell (pointing down) two 45° steps give an arrow pointing left.
hints: How much does the arrow turn from one column to the next?
Check that the same rule works in every row.

levels.title: Shrinking Rows
levels.explanation: Each row contains a circle, a square and a triangle once, and the shapes get smaller from the top row to the bottom row.
hints: Compare sizes from top to bottom.
Which shape is still missing from the bottom row?

levels.title: Two Latin Squares
levels.explanation: Shapes and colours each follow their own once-per-row, once-per-column pattern. The missing cell needs the shape and the colour that are absent from both its row and its column.
hints: Solve the shape first, ignoring colour.
Then solve the colour, ignoring shape.

levels.title: Overlay
levels.explanation: The third cell of each row is the first two cells laid on top of each other. In the bottom row that gives three lines.
hints: Compare the top row's third cell with its first two cells.
Nothing disappears; lines are only combined.

levels.title: Shape and Count
levels.explanation: Two rules run together: the shape cycles circle → square → triangle, and every figure has one more item than the one before.
hints: Look at the shapes and the number of items separately.
After a square comes a triangle; after 5 items come 6.

levels.title: Turn and Grow
levels.explanation: The flag turns 45° clockwise and grows by the same amount at every step.
hints: Treat direction and size as two separate patterns.
Both change by the same amount every step.

levels.title: Three Independent Rules
levels.explanation: Three rules apply at once: each row and column has one circle, square and triangle; each row and column has one navy, teal and gold figure; and every column has one more item than the column to its left.
hints: Solve shape, colour and count one at a time.
The third column always has three items.

levels.title: Dots and Sides
levels.prompt: Four figures share a hidden property. Which one does not?
levels.explanation: In four figures the number of dots equals the number of sides of the shape around them. The octagon has 8 sides but holds only 7 dots.
hints: Count the dots and the sides in each figure.
Is there a link between the two numbers?

levels.title: Matching Trio
levels.prompt: The top figures obey the same hidden rules; the bottom figures each break one. Which option obeys the rules?
levels.explanation: A figure follows the rules when it has exactly three shapes and all of them share one colour. The counter-examples have mixed colours, two shapes or four shapes.
hints: Count the shapes in the figures that follow the rules.
Then compare their colours.

levels.title: Turn, Paint, Turn, Paint
levels.explanation: Two changes take turns: first the arrow turns 90° clockwise, then it switches colour, then it turns again, and so on. The last step was a turn, so the next step is a colour switch.
hints: Look at what changes between each pair of neighbours.
Only one thing changes at a time, and the two changes alternate.

levels.title: Shape, Turn, Colour
levels.explanation: Each column keeps one shape, each row turns its figures by the same amount (0°, 90°, 180°), and each row and column contains navy, teal and gold once.
hints: Read the columns for shape and the rows for direction.
Which colour is missing from the middle row?

levels.title: Turn and Swap
levels.prompt: The same change turns each figure into its partner. Which figure completes the last pair?
levels.explanation: The pair is turned a quarter turn clockwise and its two colours are swapped. Applying both changes to the third figure gives the answer.
hints: Two things change between the first two figures.
Check positions as well as colours.

levels.title: Independent Motion
levels.explanation: The chevron turns 45° counter-clockwise at each step, while the coral dot walks one cell clockwise around the edge of the board. The two motions are independent.
hints: Follow the chevron and the dot separately.
Each moves by the same amount every step.

levels.title: Both Conditions
levels.prompt: The top figures obey the same hidden rules; the bottom figures each break one. Which option obeys the rules?
levels.explanation: Figures follow the rules when they contain at least one triangle and an odd number of shapes. Each counter-example fails exactly one of these conditions.
hints: What do all the top figures contain?
Now count the shapes in each top figure.

levels.title: Facing Outwards
levels.explanation: The arrow moves one cell clockwise around the edge and turns 45° clockwise each step, so it always points away from the centre.
hints: Where does the arrow point relative to the middle of the board?
Moving and turning happen together, at the same pace.

levels.title: Merging Shapes
levels.explanation: In every row the third figure is the first two figures drawn on top of each other.
hints: Look at what the third cell of the top row contains.
Nothing is removed, and nothing new is added.

levels.title: Take Away
levels.explanation: In every row the dots in the middle cell are removed from the first cell; what remains appears in the third cell.
hints: Compare the first and third cells of the top row.
Which dots disappeared, and where were they shown?

levels.title: What Differs Remains
levels.explanation: Lines that appear in both of the first two cells cancel out; lines that appear in only one of them are kept in the third cell.
hints: In the top row, which line is shared by the first two cells?
Shared lines vanish; the rest survive.

levels.title: Build and Rebuild
levels.prompt: Apply every step in order. What is the result?
levels.explanation: Turn the group a quarter turn clockwise, remove the square, add a coral L-shape at the top edge, then mirror everything left–right — the new L-shape is mirrored too.
hints: Steps that add or remove shapes change what later steps act on.
After the final mirror, which way does the added L-shape face?

levels.title: Inside Out
levels.explanation: The three nested shapes trade places in a cycle: at each step the outer shape becomes the inner one, and the others move one layer outwards.
hints: Follow one shape, such as the navy circle, through the layers.
The order of the layers repeats every three steps.

levels.title: Two Clocks
levels.explanation: Direction repeats every three steps (up, right, down) while colour repeats every four (navy, teal, gold, coral). Each cycle continues independently.
hints: Find how often the direction repeats.
Then, separately, find how often the colour repeats.

levels.title: Order Matters
levels.prompt: Which rule turns every left figure into its right figure?
levels.explanation: Each figure is turned a quarter turn clockwise and then mirrored left–right. Doing the same two steps in the other order gives a different result.
hints: Find a turn and a mirror that together produce the right-hand flag.
Test the order of the two steps on the flag.

levels.title: Clockwork
levels.explanation: Along each row the coral dot moves one cell clockwise around the edge while the hand turns 45° clockwise. Each row starts two cells and 45° further on.
hints: Treat the dot and the hand as two separate rules.
A line looks the same after a half turn.

levels.title: Assembly Line
levels.prompt: Apply every step in order. What is the result?
levels.explanation: Turn the group a quarter turn clockwise, remove the gold square, swap navy and teal, then mirror top–bottom. Keep track of colours and positions separately.
hints: Work through one step at a time; draw it if needed.
A colour swap changes colours only, not positions.

levels.title: Sum and Shape
levels.explanation: In each row the third cell holds as many items as the first two together, and each row and column holds circles, squares and triangles once each.
hints: Count the items across the top row.
Then work out which shape is missing from the bottom row.

levels.title: Two Fewer
levels.explanation: Each shape has one more side than the last, and the number of dots inside is always two less than the number of sides. A heptagon (7 sides) therefore holds 5 dots.
hints: Count both the sides and the dots in every figure.
Is there a fixed link between the two numbers?

levels.title: Like Within Like
levels.prompt: The top figures obey the same hidden rules; the bottom figures each break one. Which option obeys the rules?
levels.explanation: A figure follows the rule when it is a single outlined shape holding one smaller solid copy of the same shape inside it. Counter-examples use a different inner shape, put the copy outside, or hold two copies.
hints: Compare the inner shape with the outer shape in each top figure.
Check where the small shape sits and how many there are.

levels.title: Sides Add Up
levels.prompt: Four figures share a hidden property. Which one does not?
levels.explanation: In four figures the sides of the two small shapes add up to the sides of the large shape (3+3=6, 4+4=8, 3+4=7, 5+3=8). In the odd figure 4+4 makes 8, but the heptagon has only 7 sides.
hints: Count the sides of every shape.
Compare the small shapes' total with the large shape.

levels.title: Three at Once
levels.explanation: Three independent rules: the arrow turns 90° clockwise, the coral circle moves one cell right along the bottom row (wrapping around), and the square cycles navy → teal → gold.
hints: Give each of the three pieces its own rule.
Check every piece in your chosen answer.

levels.title: Growing Gaps
levels.explanation: The gaps grow by one each time: +1, +2, +3, so the next gap is +4 and 7 + 4 = 11 dots.
hints: Write down how many dots are added at each step.
Look at how the differences themselves change.

levels.title: Add the Last Two
levels.explanation: Each count is the sum of the two counts before it: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5 — so the next figure has 3 + 5 = 8 triangles.
hints: The first two figures are identical — that is a clue.
Try combining two neighbouring counts.

levels.title: Adding Angles
levels.explanation: Measured clockwise from 'up', the third arrow's angle in each row is the sum of the first two: 45°+90°=135°, 90°+45°=135°, 180°+90°=270°.
hints: Express each arrow as an angle turned clockwise from pointing up.
Combine the first two angles of each row.

levels.title: Column Cancel
levels.explanation: Read down each column: squares that appear in both the top and middle cells cancel out, and squares that appear in only one of them drop to the bottom cell.
hints: The rows hide nothing — try the columns.
Shared squares vanish; unique squares survive.

levels.title: Accelerating Turn
levels.explanation: The turns grow by 45° each step (45°, 90°, 135°, 180°), so the next turn is 225°; meanwhile the fill alternates solid and outlined.
hints: Measure how far the flag turns between neighbours.
The turning amount itself follows a pattern.

levels.title: Sides to Dots
levels.prompt: Every row follows the same rule. Which figure completes the last row?
levels.explanation: Each row translates a shape into dots: the number of dots on the right equals the number of sides of the shape on the left. A hexagon has six sides.
hints: Compare the left and right cells of the top row.
What could the shape tell you about the number of dots?

levels.title: Diagonal Mirror
levels.prompt: Which rule turns every left figure into its right figure?
levels.explanation: Each figure is reflected in the diagonal running from bottom-left to top-right (╱): the top-left area swaps with the bottom-right, and every shape is flipped across that line.
hints: A quarter turn moves everything; a diagonal mirror flips it. Test both on the flag.
Look at which corners swap places in the second example.

levels.title: Five Steps
levels.prompt: Apply every step in order. What is the result?
levels.explanation: Turn, mirror top–bottom and turn again combine into one top–bottom mirror; the colour swap exchanges navy and gold, and the final step turns solid shapes outlined and outlined shapes solid (the striped triangle is unaffected).
hints: Handle geometry and colour separately.
Three geometric steps can collapse into one simpler move.

levels.title: Follow the Leader
levels.explanation: The coral circle moves 1, then 2, then 3 cells clockwise, so next it moves 4 cells. The navy square always steps into the cell the circle has just left.
hints: The square's path depends on the circle's path.
Where was the circle one step earlier?

levels.title: Uniform with One Accent
levels.prompt: The top figures obey the same hidden rules; the bottom figures each break one. Which option obeys the rules?
levels.explanation: Figures follow the rules when every shape has the same fill and exactly one shape is coral. Counter-examples mix fills, have two coral shapes, or have none.
hints: Look at the fills inside each top figure.
Then count the coral shapes.

levels.title: Shape, Turn and Fill
levels.explanation: Each row and column contains the flag, the L-shape and the right triangle once; each column turns its figures by the same amount (0°, 90°, 180°); each row has its own fill.
hints: Use the rows for fill, the columns for direction.
Which shape is missing from the bottom row?

levels.title: Triple Change
levels.prompt: The same change turns each figure into its partner. Which figure completes the last pair?
levels.explanation: Three changes happen together: a half turn, solid and outlined fills trade places, and teal and coral swap colours.
hints: List every difference between the first two figures.
Check position, fill and colour.

levels.title: Two Threads
levels.explanation: Two sequences are woven together. Circles go 2, 4, 6 (adding two); squares go 9, 8, 7 (taking one). The next figure continues the circle thread with 8.
hints: Look at every other figure.
Treat circles and squares as two separate sequences.

levels.title: Majority Rule
levels.prompt: Four figures share a hidden property. Which one does not?
levels.explanation: In four figures solid shapes outnumber outlined shapes. In the odd figure only one of the three shapes is solid.
hints: Ignore shapes and colours; look only at fills.
Compare how many shapes are solid with how many are outlined.

levels.title: Row Totals
levels.explanation: Each row uses one shape, its third cell holds the total of the first two cells, and each row and column contains navy, teal and gold once.
hints: Work out the count first.
Then use rows and columns to settle the colour.

levels.title: Satellites
levels.explanation: Three rules run in parallel: the arrow turns 90° clockwise, its colour cycles navy → teal → gold, and one more coral satellite joins the ring (filling clockwise from the top-left).
hints: Track the arrow's direction, the arrow's colour and the satellites separately.
Each rule moves forward by exactly one step per figure.

levels.title: Four Dimensions
levels.explanation: Four rules: each row and column holds an arrow, a flag and a chevron once; colours form their own once-per-row-and-column pattern; each column has its own fill; and each row turns its figures 45° further than the row above.
hints: Solve one attribute at a time: shape, colour, fill, direction.
Direction depends only on the row; fill only on the column.

levels.title: Long Journey
levels.prompt: Apply every step in order. What is the result?
levels.explanation: Moves and turns of the whole board both carry the pieces: after shifting right, turning, shifting up, mirroring and turning back, the arrow ends at the left-middle cell pointing down and the square at the bottom-middle; the last step empties their fills.
hints: Track the two pieces' cells after every step.
A turn of the board moves edge cells around the centre.

levels.title: Uneven Steps
levels.explanation: The coral dot alternates between moving one cell and two cells clockwise around the edge (+1, +2, +1, +2…), while the flag turns 90° counter-clockwise every step.
hints: Measure how far the dot moves each time.
The step sizes repeat in a short rhythm.

levels.title: Slide and Spin
levels.prompt: The same change turns each figure into its partner. Which figure completes the last pair?
levels.explanation: Each board is slid one cell to the right and then turned a quarter turn clockwise. The slide happens before the turn, so pieces travel around the centre afterwards.
hints: Use both examples to pin down the rule.
Try one move, then one turn of the whole board.

levels.title: Removal Order
levels.explanation: In every row the shapes shown in the middle cell are taken away from the first cell, leaving the third cell. In the bottom row the triangle and the diamond are removed.
hints: Compare the first and last cells of the top row.
The middle cell lists what disappears.

levels.title: Three Conditions
levels.prompt: The top figures obey the same hidden rules; the bottom figures each break one. Which option obeys the rules?
levels.explanation: A figure obeys the rules when it has an odd number of shapes, includes at least one coral shape, and all its shapes share one fill. Each counter-example breaks exactly one condition.
hints: Find what every top figure has in common — there are three things.
Check count, colour and fill for each option.

levels.title: Pinwheels
levels.prompt: Four figures share a hidden property. Which one does not?
levels.explanation: Four figures look the same after a quarter turn — they are pinwheels. The odd figure only repeats after a full turn because its L-shapes alternate between two orientations.
hints: Imagine turning each figure by 90°.
Which figure would look different after the turn?

levels.title: Turn or Count
levels.explanation: Two actions alternate: turn the arrow 90° clockwise, then add a dot, then turn again, then add a dot… The last action was a turn, so the next action adds a fourth dot.
hints: Only one thing changes between neighbouring figures.
Which change happened last?

levels.title: Side Arithmetic
levels.explanation: In every row the number of sides of the third shape is the total of the first two shapes' sides: 3+3=6, 4+3=7, 5+3=8. Colours follow a once-per-row-and-column pattern.
hints: Count the sides of every shape in the top row.
Then decide the colour from the row and column.

levels.title: Four Clocks
levels.explanation: Four rules at once: the arrow turns 45° clockwise and grows a little every step; the dot walks one cell clockwise around the edge; and the dot's colour cycles coral → teal → gold.
hints: There are four independent changes. List them before choosing.
Check size, direction, position and colour for every option.

levels.title: Double Cancel
levels.explanation: Lines cancel in both directions: in every row, and in every column, the third cell keeps only the lines that appear in exactly one of the first two cells.
hints: Start with the top row, then check that the same rule works down the columns.
Shared lines disappear; unique lines remain.

levels.title: The Long Program
levels.prompt: Apply every step in order. What is the result?
levels.explanation: Follow all six instructions in order. The diagonal mirror and quarter turn combine into a left–right mirror; removing the circle and adding the central star change the pieces; gold and coral swap; finally every solid shape becomes outlined and vice versa — including the new star.
hints: Shapes added late are affected only by later steps.
Two of the geometric steps can be merged into one simpler move.

levels.title: Exact Census
levels.prompt: The top figures obey the same hidden rules; the bottom figures each break one. Which option obeys the rules?
levels.explanation: Valid figures are outlined polygons holding exactly as many coral dots as the polygon has sides. Counter-examples have the wrong number of dots, a solid polygon, or dots of the wrong colour.
hints: Compare the dots with the shape that contains them.
Fill and dot colour matter too.

levels.title: Hidden Agreement
levels.prompt: Four figures share a hidden property. Which one does not?
levels.explanation: In four figures the small shapes inside share the colour of the large shape around them. In the odd figure the inner shapes are a different colour from their container.
hints: Shapes, counts and positions all vary freely — they are distractions.
Compare the inside with the outside of each figure.

levels.title: Name the Program
levels.prompt: Which rule turns every left figure into its right figure?
levels.explanation: Each figure is turned a quarter turn clockwise, its teal and gold parts swap colours, and solid and outlined fills trade places. Every other option fails on at least one of the two examples.
hints: Check each option against both examples, not just the first.
Look at position, colour and fill separately.

options.label: Rotate 90° counter-clockwise, then swap teal and gold, then invert fill
Rotate 90° clockwise, then swap teal and gold
Mirror across the ╲ diagonal, then swap teal and gold, then invert fill
Rotate 90° clockwise, then swap teal and gold, then invert fill

levels.title: Spiral Growth
levels.explanation: Each count is the sum of the previous two (1, 1, 2, 3, 5 → 8); all arrows turn 90° clockwise every step; and the colour alternates navy and teal.
hints: Three rules: count, direction and colour.
The first two counts are equal — what kind of sequence starts that way?

levels.title: Composite Matrix
levels.explanation: Three rules: each row and column holds the flag, the L-shape and the arrow once; the third column's direction is the sum of the first two directions (measured clockwise from up); and every column has one more item than the column to its left.
hints: Directions add along each row.
The item count depends only on the column.

levels.title: Three-Part Program
levels.prompt: The same change turns each figure into its partner. Which figure completes the last pair?
levels.explanation: Both examples apply the same program: move everything one cell down, turn the board half a turn, then swap navy and coral. Applied to the last board, the L-shape lands on the left edge.
hints: Use both examples to rule out simpler programs.
Find the move, the turn and the colour change.

levels.title: Mastermind
levels.explanation: Everything comes together: the number of arrows in the third column is the sum of the first two; each step to the right turns the arrows 90° clockwise and each step down adds 45°; and navy, teal and gold appear once in every row and column.
hints: Count first, then direction, then colour.
Direction depends on both the row and the column.
